mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate environment reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 6.5% over a 3-month period signals strengthening labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls below 6.5% but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates robust demand conditions, which are associated with rising corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both series are above their 3-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 100, the economy is in a supply contraction phase, which typically leads to higher inflation and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO falls below 100 but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5% YoY but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market conditions, as measured by a high level of employment growth (PAYEMS), consistently support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS grows by more than 100k in a month but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDPC1 growth rate below 2.0% but positive), a decline in residential construction (HOUST) signals weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth < 2.0% and >0%), HOUST declines >0.5% MoM but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a supply shock coupled with labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO falls and UNRATE rises but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.
